questiontext.text:
Arrange the following historical milestones in the development of organic chemistry in the correct chronological order (earliest to latest):

P. Synthesis of acetic acid by Kolbe from inorganic sources
Q. Proposal of the 'vital force' theory by Berzilius
R. Synthesis of methane by Berthelot from inorganic sources
S. Synthesis of urea from ammonium cyanate by F. Wohler

Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Modern organic chemistry evolved through the rejection of the 'vital force' theory after key laboratory syntheses of organic compounds from inorganic precursors.

Step 2: Chronological Ordering
First, Berzilius proposed that a 'vital force' was responsible for the formation of organic compounds. In 1828, F. Wohler disproved this notion by synthesising urea from ammonium cyanate. Later, Kolbe achieved the synthesis of acetic acid in 1845, followed by Berthelot's synthesis of methane in 1856.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct chronological order from earliest to latest is Q → S → P → R.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANICCHEMISTRY_SEQUENCING_Q02 - Decreasing IUPAC priority order of functional groups

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following functional groups in the correct decreasing order of IUPAC priority (highest priority first) when naming polyfunctional organic compounds:

P. \(-\mathrm{OH}\)
Q. \(-\mathrm{COOH}\)
R. \(-\mathrm{CHO}\)
S. \(-\mathrm{COOR}\)

Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In polyfunctional organic compounds, one functional group is chosen as the principal functional group based on a fixed IUPAC order of preference, while the remaining groups are treated as prefix substituents.

Step 2: Ordering by Priority
According to the IUPAC priority sequence, carboxylic acids (\(-\mathrm{COOH}\)) hold the highest priority among these four groups, followed by esters (\(-\mathrm{COOR}\)), then aldehydes (\(-\mathrm{CHO}\)), and finally alcohols (\(-\mathrm{OH}\)).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Thus, the correct decreasing order of priority is Q → S → R → P.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANICCHEMISTRY_SEQUENCING_Q03 - IUPAC naming steps for branched alkanes

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following steps in the correct logical sequence for deriving the IUPAC name of a branched-chain alkane:

P. Number the carbon atoms of the parent chain so that the branched carbon atoms get the lowest possible numbers.
Q. Identify the longest continuous carbon chain in the molecule as the parent chain.
R. Prefix the names of different alkyl substituents in alphabetical order to the parent alkane name.
S. Determine the locant numbers and identities of all alkyl substituents attached to the parent chain.

Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
IUPAC nomenclature of branched-chain alkanes follows a systematic rule-based order starting from chain selection and ending with name assembly.

Step 2: Ordering the Steps
First, the longest continuous carbon chain is identified as the parent chain. Second, the parent chain is numbered from the end that gives the lowest possible locants to the branched carbons. Third, the positions and identities of the alkyl substituents are determined. Finally, the substituent names are arranged in alphabetical order as prefixes to the parent alkane name.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the correct logical sequence is Q → P → S → R.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANICCHEMISTRY_SEQUENCING_Q04 - Steps in Lassaigne's test for nitrogen

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following experimental steps in the correct chronological order for detecting nitrogen in an organic compound using Lassaigne's test:

P. Acidify with concentrated \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\) to oxidise some \(\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}\) to \(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}\) and obtain a Prussian blue colour.
Q. Fuse the organic compound with metallic sodium to convert covalent carbon and nitrogen into ionic \(\mathrm{NaCN}\).
R. Boil the extract with iron(II) sulphate (\(\mathrm{FeSO}_4\)) to form sodium hexacyanidoferrate(II).
S. Boil the fused mass with distilled water and filter to prepare the sodium fusion extract.

Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Lassaigne's test converts covalently bonded elements in an organic compound into water-soluble ionic sodium salts, which then undergo characteristic inorganic qualitative reactions.

Step 2: Ordering the Experimental Steps
First, the organic compound is fused with metallic sodium to form \(\mathrm{NaCN}\). Second, the fused mass is boiled with distilled water to obtain the sodium fusion extract. Third, the extract is boiled with \(\mathrm{FeSO}_4\) so that \(\mathrm{CN}^-\) reacts with \(\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}\) to form \([\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]^{4-}\). Finally, acidification with concentrated \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\) oxidises some \(\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}\) to \(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}\), forming Prussian blue \(\mathrm{Fe}_4[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]_3 \cdot x\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Hence, the correct chronological sequence is Q → S → R → P.

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following steps in the correct sequence for purifying an impure solid organic compound by crystallisation:

P. Cool the hot, nearly saturated solution so that the pure compound crystallises out.
Q. Dissolve the impure compound in a suitable solvent in which it is sparingly soluble at room temperature but appreciably soluble at higher temperature.
R. Filter the hot solution (after treating with activated charcoal if coloured impurities are present) and concentrate to obtain a nearly saturated solution.
S. Remove the pure crystals from the mother liquor by filtration and dry them.

Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Crystallisation relies on the temperature-dependent difference in solubility between the organic compound and its impurities in a chosen solvent.

Step 2: Ordering the Steps
First, the impure solid is dissolved in a suitable hot solvent where it has high solubility. Next, insoluble and coloured impurities (via activated charcoal) are removed by hot filtration, and the solution is concentrated to near saturation. Then, cooling the solution causes the pure compound to crystallise out while soluble impurities remain in the mother liquor. Finally, the crystals are separated by filtration.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Thus, the correct sequence is Q → R → P → S.

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following steps in the correct chronological order for separating an organic compound from an aqueous medium by differential extraction:

P. Allow the mixture in the separatory funnel to settle into two distinct immiscible layers.
Q. Shake the aqueous solution with an immiscible organic solvent in which the organic compound is more soluble.
R. Remove the organic solvent by distillation or evaporation to recover the organic compound.
S. Separate the organic layer from the aqueous layer using the stopcock of the separatory funnel.

Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Differential extraction partitions an organic solute from water into an immiscible organic solvent based on higher solubility in the organic phase.

Step 2: Ordering the Steps
First, the aqueous solution is shaken with the immiscible organic solvent inside a separatory funnel so the compound transfers into the organic phase. Second, the mixture is allowed to stand so two distinct layers form. Third, the two layers are separated via the stopcock. Finally, the organic solvent is removed by distillation or evaporation to isolate the compound.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the correct chronological order is Q → P → S → R.

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following sequential stages in the direct quantitative estimation of oxygen in an organic compound:

P. Pass the gaseous products containing \(\mathrm{O}_2\) over red-hot coke at \(1373\text{ K}\) to convert all oxygen into carbon monoxide (\(\mathrm{CO}\)).
Q. Decompose a known mass of the organic compound by heating in a stream of nitrogen gas to liberate \(\mathrm{O}_2\) and other gaseous products.
R. Measure the mass of \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) (or \(\mathrm{I}_2\)) formed to calculate the percentage of oxygen in the compound.
S. Pass the carbon monoxide mixture through warm iodine pentoxide (\(\mathrm{I}_2\mathrm{O}_5\)) to oxidise \(\mathrm{CO}\) into \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) and \(\mathrm{I}_2\).

Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Direct estimation of oxygen converts all oxygen in an organic sample into \(\mathrm{CO}\), and then quantitatively oxidises \(\mathrm{CO}\) to \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) and \(\mathrm{I}_2\) using \(\mathrm{I}_2\mathrm{O}_5\).

Step 2: Ordering the Chemical Stages
First, a definite mass of the organic compound is decomposed by heating in a stream of nitrogen gas to liberate \(\mathrm{O}_2\). Second, the gaseous mixture is passed over red-hot coke at \(1373\text{ K}\), converting all \(\mathrm{O}_2\) into \(\mathrm{CO}\) (\(2\mathrm{C} + \mathrm{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\mathrm{CO}\)). Third, the \(\mathrm{CO}\) is passed through warm \(\mathrm{I}_2\mathrm{O}_5\), producing \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) and \(\mathrm{I}_2\) (\(\mathrm{I}_2\mathrm{O}_5 + 5\mathrm{CO} \rightarrow \mathrm{I}_2 + 5\mathrm{CO}_2\)). Finally, the amount of \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) (or \(\mathrm{I}_2\)) is measured to compute the percentage of oxygen.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Thus, the correct sequence is Q → P → S → R.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANICCHEMISTRY_SEQUENCING_Q08 - Stages in Kjeldahl's method for nitrogen

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following procedural stages of Kjeldahl's method for the quantitative estimation of nitrogen in the correct chronological order:

P. Absorb the evolved ammonia gas in a known excess volume of standard \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\) solution.
Q. Heat the nitrogen-containing organic compound with concentrated \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\) to convert nitrogen into ammonium sulphate.
R. Titrate the unreacted excess \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\) with a standard \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) solution to determine the acid consumed by ammonia.
S. Heat the resulting acid mixture with excess \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) to liberate ammonia gas.

Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Kjeldahl's method converts organic nitrogen into ammonium sulphate, liberates it as ammonia gas, and quantifies it by back-titration of a standard acid.

Step 2: Ordering the Procedural Stages
First, the organic compound is digested by heating with concentrated \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\) so that nitrogen is converted to \((\mathrm{NH}_4)_2\mathrm{SO}_4\). Second, the digested mixture is heated with excess \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) to liberate \(\mathrm{NH}_3\) gas. Third, the evolved \(\mathrm{NH}_3\) is absorbed in a known excess of standard \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\). Finally, the remaining unreacted \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\) is titrated with standard \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) to find the amount of acid neutralised by \(\mathrm{NH}_3\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Hence, the correct chronological sequence is Q → S → P → R.
